MCQs.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of microorganism?
Who developed the process of pasteurization to kill harmful bacteria in milk?
Which statement best describes bacteria?
options: A) They are the smallest microorganisms and need a host to grow
B) They are single-celled organisms found in soil, water and even the body
C) They are multicellular organisms like mushrooms
D) They only cause diseases and have no benefits
MCQs.answer: B) They are single-celled organisms found in soil, water and even the body

MCQs.question: Why must viruses live inside the cells of other living things?
options: D) To produce their own food

MCQs.question: A student wants to turn warm milk into yoghurt at home. Which microorganism should be added to the milk?
During fermentation, yeast changes sugar into carbon dioxide, which makes bread rise. What is yeast an example of?
Which of these diseases is caused by a virus?
Which of these is an example of a fungal infection?
A boy shakes hands with a sick classmate and later touches his own face. He then falls sick with a cold. What does this best show?
options: A) A non-contagious disease spreading through genetics
B) A contagious disease spreading through contact
C) A non-contagious disease spreading through air
D) A contagious disease spreading through sunlight
MCQs.answer: B) A contagious disease spreading through contact

MCQs.question: Which of the following is a non-contagious disease?
Which statement correctly tells apart contagious and non-contagious diseases?
options: A) Contagious diseases spread between people; non-contagious diseases are caused by things like genetics or poor nutrition
B) Contagious diseases are always caused by fungi only
C) Non-contagious diseases spread through coughing and sneezing
D) Both types of diseases spread in exactly the same way
MCQs.answer: A) Contagious diseases spread between people; non-contagious diseases are caused by things like genetics or poor nutrition

MCQs.question: During a viral outbreak at school, a student wore a mask and kept distance from sick classmates. Which type of disease was she trying to prevent from spreading?
How does washing hands with soap help prevent the spread of disease?
options: A) It kills every virus instantly
B) It removes germs that could be transferred to the mouth, nose or eyes
C) It changes the colour of germs so they are harmless
D) It only makes the skin feel softer
MCQs.answer: B) It removes germs that could be transferred to the mouth, nose or eyes

MCQs.question: If a whole community gets vaccinated against polio, what is the most likely effect on the spread of the disease?
options: A) The disease spreads faster among people
B) The disease spreads less because more people are protected
C) The vaccine causes the disease to appear in everyone
D) There is no change at all in the disease's spread
MCQs.answer: B) The disease spreads less because more people are protected

MCQs.question: What is the main purpose of a vaccine?
options: A) To cure a disease immediately after it appears
B) To train the immune system to recognise and fight a disease
C) To act as a pain reliever for sick people
D) To provide extra nutrition to the body
MCQs.answer: B) To train the immune system to recognise and fight a disease

MCQs.question: Which scientist discovered penicillin after noticing a mould killing bacteria in his petri dish?
What role do microorganisms play in decomposition?
options: A) They prevent dead material from breaking down
B) They break down dead plants and animals into nutrient-rich soil
C) They turn soil directly into fossil fuels
D) They have no effect on dead matter
MCQs.answer: B) They break down dead plants and animals into nutrient-rich soil

MCQs.question: A farmer notices that fallen leaves in his field slowly turn into rich soil over many weeks. Which process, mainly carried out by microorganisms, explains this?
Which of these is an example of fermentation?
options: A) Mould growing on old bread
B) Yeast turning sugar into carbon dioxide to make bread rise
C) A virus infecting a healthy cell
D) Washing hands with soap and water
MCQs.answer: B) Yeast turning sugar into carbon dioxide to make bread rise

Logical Reasoning.main_question: Read each situation and attempt ANY TWO of the three situations below. For each situation chosen, answer any two of its three questions. Give answers with logical reasons.
Logical Reasoning.question: During a class activity, Ali sprayed coloured water mixed with glitter into the air to represent germs from a sneeze. Some glitter landed on the table and on his classmates' hands. One classmate shook hands with three different friends, and one friend touched his own face. Later, some students washed their hands with soap and water, while others only rinsed with plain water.
questions: a) Why did the glitter end up on the hands of students who never touched the sprayed area directly?
b) What would most likely happen if the student who touched his face did not wash his hands afterward?
c) Why might rinsing with only water be less effective than washing with soap and water in removing the glitter (germs)?
Logical Reasoning.answer: a) Germs/glitter spread from person to person through touch (handshakes) and contaminated surfaces. b) The germs could enter his body through his face (eyes/nose/mouth) and make him sick. c) Soap breaks down and removes germs/dirt from the skin more effectively than plain water, which only loosens some particles.

points.text: Correct reasoning for the first chosen question showing understanding of germ transmission through contact
Correct reasoning for the second chosen question linking cause and effect of disease spread
Correct use of scientific terms such as 'germs', 'contagious' or 'transmission'

accept: Any two of the three sub-answers reasoned logically with correct cause-and-effe…
scheme.common_error: Child says germs only spread by air and ignores the role of touch/contact shown in the situation

Logical Reasoning.main_question: Read each situation and attempt ANY TWO of the three situations below. For each situation chosen, answer any two of its three questions. Give answers with logical reasons.
Logical Reasoning.question: Sara mixed a spoonful of plain yoghurt into warm milk and kept it in a warm place for two days. At the same time, she placed a piece of bread and a piece of fruit in two separate open jars and left them on a shelf for a week.
questions: a) Why did the milk change into yoghurt after being left in a warm place with the added yoghurt?
b) What changes would Sara most likely observe on the bread and fruit after a week, and why?
c) If Sara had kept the milk in the fridge instead of a warm place, would it still turn into yoghurt? Why or why not?
Logical Reasoning.answer: a) The bacteria from the added yoghurt feed on the sugars in warm milk and produce lactic acid, which turns the milk into yoghurt. b) Mould (a fungus) would likely grow on the bread and fruit, causing them to decompose, because microorganisms break down organic matter over time. c) No, because bacteria grow and multiply best in warm conditions; the cold would slow down or stop their activity.

points.text: Correct reasoning for the first chosen question explaining the role of bacteria in fermentation
Correct reasoning for the second chosen question explaining decomposition by fungi/microorganisms
Correct use of scientific terms such as 'fermentation', 'bacteria' or 'decomposition'

accept: Any two of the three sub-answers reasoned logically using the concepts of ferme…
scheme.common_error: Child thinks the milk changes on its own without connecting the role of the added bacteria

Logical Reasoning.main_question: Read each situation and attempt ANY TWO of the three situations below. For each situation chosen, answer any two of its three questions. Give answers with logical reasons.
Logical Reasoning.question: Hassan left one iron nail outside in the rain for several days and kept another iron nail of the same type in a dry box indoors. After a week, he compared both nails.
questions: a) What difference would Hassan most likely notice between the two nails?
b) Why did the nail left outside change while the other one did not?
c) What could Hassan do to protect iron objects from this kind of change?
Logical Reasoning.answer: a) The nail left outside would turn reddish-brown and rough (rusted), while the dry one would stay shiny and unchanged. b) The outdoor nail was exposed to both water and air, which causes iron to rust, while the indoor nail was kept dry and away from moisture. c) He could paint, oil, or coat the iron with a protective layer, or keep it away from water and moisture.

points.text: Correct reasoning for the first chosen question identifying the visible change (rusting)
Correct reasoning for the second chosen question linking rusting to presence of water and air
Correct use of scientific term 'rust' or 'rusting'

accept: Any two of the three sub-answers reasoned logically using the cause of rusting…
scheme.common_error: Child says the nail changed only because of dirt, without connecting it to water and air causing rust

Brief Answers.question: Why do we need to add a small amount of yoghurt to warm milk to make more yoghurt?

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail. (Attempt any 2)
Long Question.question: Imagine your school wants to prevent a contagious viral outbreak like the flu or COVID-19. Describe a detailed action plan including at least three preventive measures and explain why each measure is effective.
Long Question.answer: To prevent a viral outbreak, the school should implement three main measures. First, enforce regular handwashing with soap and water; this is effective because it removes and kills germs that transfer from touching contaminated surfaces. Second, require wearing masks; this blocks airborne droplets from sneezing or coughing, stopping the virus from entering the air. Third, maintain social distancing and avoid casual contact like handshakes; this prevents the virus from spreading through direct human contact.

points.text: First preventive measure and why it is effective
Second preventive measure and why it is effective
Third preventive measure and why it is effective

accept: Using sanitisers, vaccination drives, isolating sick students, with correct sci…
scheme.common_error: Listing measures without explaining why they work

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail. (Attempt any 2)
Long Question.question: Microorganisms are often thought of as harmful, but many are highly beneficial. Discuss the beneficial roles of microorganisms in both the food industry and the environment, providing specific examples for each.
Long Question.answer: Microorganisms play a crucial role in our daily lives. In the food industry, friendly bacteria are used to ferment milk, which creates yoghurt and cheese. Another example is yeast, a fungus that ferments sugar to produce carbon dioxide, making bread fluffy. In the environment, microorganisms like bacteria and fungi are nature's recyclers. They carry out decomposition by breaking down dead plants and leaves. This turns waste into nutrient-rich soil, which is essential for new plants to grow.

points.text: Explains role in food industry with an example (e.g., bacteria for yoghurt/cheese or yeast for bread)
Explains role in the environment with an example (e.g., decomposition of dead matter into soil)

accept: Mentions of phytoplankton producing oxygen, or fungi making antibiotics
scheme.common_error: Focusing only on food or only on the environment

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail. (Attempt any 2)
Long Question.question: A farmer notices that dead leaves and plants in his field eventually disappear and turn into rich soil. Explain the scientific process happening here. Identify the microorganisms responsible and discuss what would happen to the earth if this process stopped.
Long Question.answer: The scientific process happening in the farmer's field is called decomposition. It is the natural breaking down of dead organic matter. Microorganisms, primarily bacteria and fungi, are responsible for this process. They feed on the dead leaves and plants, turning them into fertile, nutrient-rich soil. If this process stopped, dead material and waste would pile up everywhere. Furthermore, the soil would lose its nutrients, making it impossible for new plants to grow, which would disrupt the entire ecosystem.

points.text: Identifies the process as decomposition
Identifies bacteria and fungi as the responsible microorganisms
Explains that it turns dead matter into nutrient-rich soil
Discusses the consequences if it stopped (waste piles up, no new plant growth)

accept: Any scientifically accurate description of the decay cycle and its importance
scheme.common_error: Failing to explain the consequences of decomposition stopping

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail. (Attempt any 2)
Long Question.question: Compare and contrast bacteria and viruses based on the text. Discuss their size differences, how they survive or grow, and give two examples of diseases caused by each.
Long Question.answer: Bacteria and viruses are both tiny microorganisms, but they have major differences. Viruses are much smaller than bacteria. For survival and growth, viruses must live inside the cells of other living hosts, whereas bacteria are single-celled organisms that can live almost anywhere, including in soil, water, and inside our bodies. Two examples of diseases caused by bacteria are food poisoning and sore throat. Two examples of diseases caused by viruses are influenza (flu) and COVID-19.

points.text: States viruses are smaller than bacteria
Explains survival differences (viruses need a host cell, bacteria can live independently)
Provides two examples of bacterial diseases
Provides two examples of viral diseases

accept: Hepatitis, polio, common cold for viruses; cholera for bacteria
scheme.common_error: Swapping the diseases caused by bacteria with those caused by viruses

Long Question.main_question: Answer the following questions in detail. (Attempt any 2)
Long Question.question: Explain the concept of vaccination. How do vaccines prepare the body's immune system, and why is it important for controlling outbreaks of contagious diseases like Polio and COVID-19?
Long Question.answer: Vaccination is a method to protect individuals from contagious diseases without them having to get sick first. Vaccines work by introducing a safe, harmless component of a disease-causing microorganism into the body. This trains the body's immune system to recognize and fight the real pathogen effectively if it ever enters the body in the future. This is crucial for controlling outbreaks of diseases like Polio and COVID-19 because when many people are vaccinated, the disease cannot spread easily from person to person, protecting the whole community.

points.text: Explains vaccines prepare the immune system without causing illness
Explains the mechanism (introducing a safe component to teach recognition)
Explains importance in controlling outbreaks (stops person-to-person spread)

accept: Descriptions using the 'Vaccine Shield' concept of community protection
scheme.common_error: Stating that vaccines kill the virus after a person is already severely sick
